description: The mock-up server of a brainstorm: one TypeScript script run with Bun (`bun scripts/mockup.ts start|stop|serve`) that shows the newest HTML file of a folder in a browser tab, guarded by a key, and writes the user's clicks on choices to a file the agent reads.
steps: `start` prints one line of JSON with `"type":"server-started"` and the fields `port`, `host`, `url_host`, `url`, `screen_dir`, `state_dir` and `idle_timeout_ms`, and returns with exit code 0 while the server goes on running.
The `url` of that line is `http://<url_host>:<port>/?key=<key>`, with an IPv6 host in square brackets.
The same line is in the file `server-info` of the state folder, which only its owner can read.

With `--dir <folder>` the session's folder is `<folder>/<a new id>/`, with the folders `content` (`screen_dir`) and `state` (`state_dir`) in it; a relative `<folder>` is taken from where the command was called, and is made when it is missing.
Without `--dir` the session's folder is under the system's temporary folder.
`--host <host>` is the address the server listens on (`127.0.0.1` when not given), and `--url-host <host>` is the host in the `url` (`localhost` for `127.0.0.1`).
`--idle-timeout-minutes <n>` sets `idle_timeout_ms` to n minutes; anything but a whole number above 0 prints a line with `error` `--idle-timeout-minutes must be a positive integer` and exits 1.
An argument it does not know prints a line with `error` `Unknown argument: <the argument>` and exits 1.

With `--foreground`, `start` does not return until the server ends, and the file `server.pid` of the state folder holds the server's process id. `start` chooses the foreground by itself on Windows and when `CODEX_CI` is set, and `--background` keeps it in the background there too; `--no-daemon` and `--daemon` are other names for the two.
`stop <session folder>` ends that session's server, prints a line with `status` `stopped`, removes `server-info`, and writes `server-stopped` in the state folder with `"reason":"stop"`.
After `stop`, a session made without `--dir` is deleted, and a session made with `--dir` keeps its folder and its screens, wherever `<folder>` lies.
`stop` for a session with no `server.pid` prints a line with `status` `not_running`; `stop` with no folder prints a line with `error` and its usage and exits 1.

When `server.pid` names a live process that is not this session's server (its command line does not carry `--brainstorm-server-id=<the id in the state folder's server-instance-id>`, or that file is missing or malformed), `stop` does not signal it, prints a line with `status` `stale_pid`, and writes `server-stopped` with `"reason":"stale_pid"`.
With no screen in `content`, `GET /` gives a page that says `Waiting for the agent to push a screen...`.
`GET /` gives the newest `.html` file of `content`, by time of change.
A screen that starts with `<!DOCTYPE` or `<html` is served as it is; any other is a fragment and is served inside the frame, its text unchanged, a `$&` in it too.
Every page served at `/` carries the browser script, and its content type is `text/html`.
A file of `content` that is no `.html`, whose name starts with a dot, that is a symbolic link, or that is a hard link to a file outside `content`, is never served as the screen.

`GET /files/<name>` gives that file of `content` with the content type of its ending; an empty name, a name that starts with a dot, a symbolic link, a hard link to a file outside, and a missing file give 404, and the server goes on.
Any other path gives 404.
A request with no key, or with a wrong `key` in the URL (a right cookie beside it too), gets 403 and a page headed `Session key required`.

`GET /?key=<the right key>` gives, not the screen, a page that puts the key into the tab's session storage as `brainstorm-session-key` and goes to `/`; the answer sets the cookie `brainstorm-key-<port>` with `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` and `Path=/`.
`GET /` and `GET /files/<name>` with that cookie and no key in the URL are served.

Every answer (200, 403, 404) carries `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`.
A WebSocket on `/` opens with the right key in the URL or the right cookie, and is refused with neither, or when its `Origin` is not `http://<the Host header>`.

A message from a browser that has a `choice` is added, as one line of JSON, to the file `events` of the state folder; a message without `choice` is not; a message that is no JSON, or is `null`, changes nothing and the server goes on.
Every message from a browser is one line of JSON with `"source":"user-event"` in the server's output, which for a server in the background is the file `server.log` of the state folder.
A new `.html` file in `content` sends `{"type":"reload"}` to every browser connected, deletes the file `events`, and gives the output line `{"type":"screen-added","file":…}`.

A change to a `.html` file that was there sends the reload and gives `{"type":"screen-updated","file":…}`, and leaves `events` as it is; a file that is no `.html`, or whose name starts with a dot, sends nothing.

After `idle_timeout_ms` (4 hours when not set) with no request that had the key, no message and no new or changed screen, the server ends by itself: it closes the open WebSockets, removes `server-info`, writes `server-stopped` with `"reason":"idle timeout"`, and its process ends; requests without the key do not put that off.

When the process named in `BRAINSTORM_OWNER_PID` has died, the server ends in the same way, with `"reason":"owner process exited"`; `start` names the coding tool's own process there, not the shell that tool used to run `start`.

A second `start` with the same `--dir`, after the first server has ended, takes the same port and the same key, so that a tab that was open connects again with its cookie; the files `.last-port` and `.last-token` in `<folder>` hold them, the second readable by its owner only.
When that port is taken, the server takes another port and a new key and leaves `.last-port` and `.last-token` as they are; when the key was given in `BRAINSTORM_TOKEN`, it exits 1 instead.

With `--open`, the user's browser is opened once, at the first screen and not before; never without `--open`, never when the server listens on another address than this machine's own, and never when a browser is already connected. `BRAINSTORM_OPEN_CMD` names the command that opens it.

A click on an element with `data-choice` sends a message with `type` `click`, the `choice`, the element's `text`, its `id` and a `timestamp`; `toggleSelect(el)` marks the element `selected`, alone among the `.option` and `.card` of its container, or beside others when the container has `data-multiselect`.
The frame's status says `Connected` while the WebSocket is open and `Reconnecting…` when it is lost; the page tries again after 500 ms, then twice as long each time, to 30 seconds at most.
After 15 seconds without the server the page shows `Companion paused` over the screen, and when the server is back it loads again by itself.

The frame has the original's classes for content: `options`, `option`, `cards`, `card`, `mockup`, `split`, `pros-cons`, `mock-nav`, `mock-sidebar`, `mock-content`, `mock-button`, `mock-input`, `placeholder`, `subtitle`, `section`, `label`.
The frame and the waiting page show `hstack v<the version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json>`, and the frame's title is `hstack brainstorm`.

What the server itself adds (the frame, the waiting page, the 403 page, the page of behaviour 22, the browser script) holds no address of another host: no image, no link, no script from the network. A screen is the agent's own and is served as it is.
The server, its two verbs and the browser's script are TypeScript run with Bun: the change adds no `.sh`, `.cjs`, `.js` or `.mjs` file, and `bun x tsc --noEmit` checks the new files and passes.

A file `LICENSE-mockup` lies beside the script, names the files it covers and holds the original's licence text with its copyright line; nothing else the change adds names the original's project or its author.
The README has a section ``### `mockup`: the mock-up server of a brainstorm`` under "Scripts", with the two verbs and their options.
`$H start` leaves a folder `mockups` of the state folder where it is, as it leaves `evidence`.

`start` with a `--host` that is not this machine's own address (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`) and without `--allow-network` starts no server, exits 1, and prints a line with `error` that names the host and says `ask the user first, then add --allow-network` and `not encrypted on a local network`. A `serve` run directly with such a `BRAINSTORM_HOST` and without `BRAINSTORM_ALLOW_NETWORK` refuses in the same way: the check is made in one place, the server itself, and `start` only hands the permission on and prints the server's refusal.

With `--allow-network`, the `server-started` line has a field `reachable_at`: one entry for each address of this machine on which the server can be reached, with its `address`, its `url` (the key in it) and its `kind`, which is `tailscale` for an address of the tailnet ranges (`100.64.0.0/10`, `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`) and `network` for any other; for a server on this machine's own address the list is empty.
The README's "Known limits" says that the Windows branch of the mock-up server has not been run on Windows.

description: Step 1 of the build loop starts with a brainstorm with the user that ends in the spec (the skill `hstack:brainstorm`), and the user may have the waiting spec grilled before the approval (the skill `hstack:grill`): the builder's first message always comes, only what was discussed and agreed is written, and the spec is handed over by its path. hstack 0.4.2.
steps: The description holds `asks the user only before the approval` and no longer `asks the user once`; it still holds `written before the code, the implementation, a gate`.

The first paragraph holds `You ask the user only before the approval: in the brainstorm, at the spec, and in a grill when the user wants one` and no longer `You ask the user once`; the sentence `After the approval nobody answers a question` is still there.
Step 1 has an item `**Brainstorm.**`, which comes before the item `**Start.**`; it holds ``invoke the `hstack:brainstorm` skill`` and `whatever other brainstorming skill the session has`.
That item holds `Never leave the brainstorm out by your own judgement` and `Your first message always comes; the user's answer to it decides whether you write the spec at once or the talk goes on`.
That item holds `Do not guess whether a person is in the session`.
That item holds `If a spec already waits for the user's approval, there is no brainstorm`.
The item `**Start.**` holds ``run `$H start` only when the brainstorm has come to the spec``, and says `$S/requirement.md` holds `every message of the user from the brainstorm, verbatim`.

The item `**The spec file.**` lists, after the request, a section `**Agreed in the brainstorm**` with `why`, `goals, what is not a goal, and what would make it a failure`, `the approaches considered and the one the user picked`, `what the user decided of the how`, and `what is left to the builder`.
That item no longer holds `It holds behaviour only` nor `no code design`; it holds `Of the how, only what the user decided` and `Write into the spec only what was discussed and agreed with the user`.

The item `**Show it.**` holds `end your turn with the path of the spec and the three choices`, names the choices as `approve it, say what to change, or have it grilled`, holds `and any point the user said to leave open`, holds `Never paste the whole text of the spec`, and no longer holds `the whole text of the spec and one line`.
The item `**The user's next message.**` has a case `A grill:`, which holds ``invoke the `hstack:grill` skill``, `the spec goes on waiting`, and `Never start a grill the user did not ask for`.
That case holds ``write it into the spec file, then `$H spec <file>` again`` and `The grill ends with a turn that gives the path, what the grill changed, and the three choices again`.
That case holds `An approval given in the middle of a grill is answered with what the grill has changed so far and the three choices; it counts when the user gives it again`.

The folder holds `SKILL.md`, `visual-companion.md`, `builder-check-prompt.md` and `LICENSE-brainstorm`; the licence names the three files it covers and holds the original's licence text with its copyright line.

The header of `SKILL.md` has `name: brainstorm`, a description that holds `Invoked by hstack:build at its step 1 and by nothing else` and ends with `invoke hstack:build, not this.`, and no `disable-model-invocation`.

`SKILL.md` holds the original's sections `## First: What Do You Actually Know?`, `## Look Before You Ask`, `## Your First Message`, `## The Conversation`, `## Play It Back`, `## Size the Work`, `## Red Flags` and `## Visual Companion`, and its parts `**Get them describing.**`, `**How it gets made.**`, `**Ground to cover.**`, `**Do recon.**`, `**Lay out the approaches.**`, `**Show, don't tell.**`, `**Spike to feel things out.**` and `**Builder check**`.

`SKILL.md` has a section `## In hstack`, which says that anyone the loop did not send must ``do nothing here and invoke `hstack:build` ``, and holds `The written design of this skill is the spec of the build loop`.

`SKILL.md` no longer holds `This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.`; it holds `Even then, send your first message before the spec` and `Their answer to it decides: write the spec at once, or go on with the conversation`.
`SKILL.md` holds neither `writing-plans` nor `design doc`; it holds `After the spec is approved, go on with step 2 of the playbook and no other skill`.
`SKILL.md` holds `Build a spike in a scratch folder outside the repository`.

`SKILL.md` has a section `## The Written Spec` and no section `## The Written Design`; the section names `Agreed in the brainstorm`, and holds `Write into the spec only what was discussed and agreed` and `The playbook's step 1 says where the spec goes and what else it holds`.
`SKILL.md` holds `Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the spec`, and no longer `the gate goes with it`; it holds `the spec is still approved before anything is built`.
The section `## Look Before You Ask` holds `the project's records`.

The part `**Builder check**` holds `Bring the "theirs" pile to your human partner in a message of its own, before you hand the spec over`, `Write an answer into the spec only when they have given it`, and ``run `$H spec <file>` before that message``.

`visual-companion.md` gives the commands ``bun "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mockup.ts" start --dir <the state folder>/mockups --open`` and ``bun "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mockup.ts" stop <session folder>``; it holds none of `start-server.sh`, `stop-server.sh`, `--project-dir` and `.gitignore`.
`visual-companion.md` holds `Ask the user before you open the server to the network`, `--allow-network`, `reachable_at`, `not encrypted on a local network` and `the machine's tailnet address`.
`visual-companion.md` holds none of the names `Codex`, `Gemini` and `Copilot`.
`builder-check-prompt.md` holds `You've been handed a spec` and no longer `design document`.
None of the three text files of the folder holds the word `superpowers`, in any letter case, and the holder of the licence's copyright line is named in none of them.

The folder holds `SKILL.md` and `LICENSE-grill`; the licence names the file it covers and holds the original's licence text with its copyright line, whose holder is named in no other file of the folder.

The header of `SKILL.md` has `name: grill`, a description that holds `Invoked by hstack:build at its step 1 and by nothing else` and ends with `invoke hstack:build, not this.`, and no `disable-model-invocation`.

`SKILL.md` holds the original's text: `Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding`, `design tree`, `frontier`, `Word each question so "yes" accepts your recommended answer`, the round's form with `❓` and `➡️`, and `Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's`.

`SKILL.md` has a section `## In hstack`, which says that anyone the loop did not send must ``do nothing here and invoke `hstack:build` ``, and holds `It runs on the spec that waits for the user's approval`.

That section holds ``Write each answer that changes the spec into the spec file, then run `$H spec <file>` again``, `Change no file but the spec`, and `When the frontier is empty and the user has confirmed, go back to the playbook`.

The text `hook-start` prints holds `It starts with a brainstorm with the user, then a spec that the user approves`, `For a build, the brainstorm is hstack's own skill, hstack:brainstorm, not another brainstorming skill`, and `after the approval, follow it to its last step`, and no longer `follow it to its last step before you reply`.

The text `hook-start` prints while a spec waits holds `approves it, asks for changes to it or asks for a grill of it`, and names the playbook's item by its name, `The user's next message`, not by a number.

What `spec <file>` prints holds `give the user the path of the spec, never its whole text`; neither it, nor the refusals of `approve` and of `phase`, nor the stop hook's reason for a spec that waits, holds `with its text` or `the spec's text`.

A turn that ends in a brainstorm (no run started, nothing changed in the repository) is not blocked by the stop hook, and `$H elapsed`, after the `start` that follows, counts no minute of it. 0.4.1 already does this (tried in a throwaway repository); a test of its own now keeps it.

A turn that ends in a grill (a spec waits; the spec file was changed and `$H spec <file>` run again; nothing else changed) is not blocked by the stop hook, and `$H elapsed` does not count the wait. 0.4.1 already does this (tried the same way); a test of its own now keeps it.
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` holds `"version": "0.4.3"`, and the README's status paragraph starts with `**Status: v0.4.3.**` and holds the words `brainstorm` and `grilled`.

In the README's skills table the `build` row holds `Asks only before the approval` and no longer `Asks once`, and there is a row for `brainstorm` and one for `grill`; the row of `skills/` in the table of folders names both.

The item `**Brainstorm.**` of the playbook holds `The user's "that is right" settles what is asked, not how it is built` and `where there is more than one way that the user would see, lay the ways out and let the user pick before you write the spec`.

The item `**The spec file.**` of the playbook says of the section "Against the record": `Raise each of them in the brainstorm; the section records what the user chose`, and no longer holds `and lettered options, the one you recommend first`.
The same item says of the section "Open points": `only what the user said to leave open`, and no longer holds `each with your proposal`.
`skills/brainstorm/visual-companion.md` holds `Stop the server when the brainstorm comes to the spec; the mock-ups stay in the state folder`.

The section `## Size the Work` of `skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md` keeps the original's two sizes, `A small change` and `A project`, and the sentence that a small change goes to the user `without the builder check`; it holds `They can override it`.
The item `**Brainstorm.**` of the playbook holds `An approval given before the spec exists is no approval: write the spec, hand it over, and wait`.
The section `## In hstack` of `skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md` holds `Invoked by the user themselves, it is the start of a build`.
The section `## In hstack` of `skills/grill/SKILL.md` holds `With no spec waiting for the user's approval, say so and do nothing`.

description: Calling the script and the brainstorm's rule on `dir`: where a builder is told how to call the script (the playbook and the feedback skill) the form with both words comes first and the shell function second; the brainstorm skill's rule that no command of the script runs but `dir` holds until the playbook's `start`, and its rule that nothing in the repository changes before the approval excepts the spec file. hstack 0.4.3.
steps: In `skills/build/SKILL.md`, the paragraph that starts with `` `H` below is `` holds ``In a command, write both words out (`bun "<the path>/scripts/hstack.ts" <verb>`)``, and these words stand before the words `shell function`.

That paragraph holds ``A shell function (`H() { bun "<the path>/scripts/hstack.ts" "$@"; }`) also works, but a coding tool may refuse a command that defines one``, holds ``a variable that holds `bun <path>` is not split into two words by every shell``, and no longer holds `call it through a shell function`.

In `skills/hstack-feedback/SKILL.md`, the paragraph that starts with `` `H` below is `` holds ``In a command, write both words out (`bun "<the path>/scripts/hstack.ts" <verb>`)``, and these words stand before the words `shell function`.

That paragraph holds ``A shell function (`H() { bun "<the path>/scripts/hstack.ts" "$@"; }`) also works, but a coding tool may refuse a command that defines one``, holds ``a variable that holds `bun <path>` is not split into two words by every shell``, and no longer holds `call it through a shell function`.
The section `## In hstack` of `skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md` holds ``until the playbook's `start` no command of the loop's script runs but `dir` `` and no longer holds `during the conversation but`.
That section holds ``From `start` on, the playbook says which command runs (`spec <file>` before a question to your human partner)``.
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` holds `"version": "0.4.3"`, and the README's status paragraph starts with `**Status: v0.4.3.**`.
The section `## In hstack` of `skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md` holds `Nothing in the repository changes before the spec is approved but the spec file itself`.
